answer: Each new identity is cut from a verified vine, entered on the lantern ledger with its dune plot; one vine places at most one identity on a dune. It locks a 50-credit bond plus a cutting fee: the kth cut from one vine costs 30+25(k-1), so 1,000 cuts from one vine cost 12,517,500 in fees plus 50,000 in bonds. A lantern auditor rejects a reused cut token or a duplicate vine on one dune, burning the clone bond. A rented-vine ring fails: mass cuts grow quadratically in fees, and the ledger exposes every clone. An honest agent cuts once, pays 80, and reclaims the bond.
